messages:
anya: Quick check before I run terraform apply — I'm adding a dedicated GPU nodepool with a capacity_reservation for predictable throughput and wiring a KMS-secured bootstrap secret for kubelet. Can someone sanity-check the tf bits and the secret mount plan?

anya: Diff snippet:```hcl
resource "aws_instance" "gpu_node" {
  instance_type = var.gpu_instance_type # p4d.24xlarge / g5dn.xlarge fallback
  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = "open"
    capacity_reservation_target {
      capacity_reservation_id = aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.gpu_cr.id
    }
  }
  tags = { role = "gpu" }
}

resource "aws_ssm_parameter" "kube_bootstrap_secret" {
  name  = "/redwood/gpu/bootstrap"
  type  = "SecureString"
  value = data.aws_kms_secrets.bootstrap_plaintext.plaintext
}
```

michael: Looks reasonable. Two quick q's: 1) do we absolutely need capacity_reservation or can we rely on instance capacity + spot fallback? 2) how is the bootstrap secret consumed on node? cloud-init?

anya: Good q's — plan is: reserved CR for prod-dedicated pool (low jitter) and a separate spot-burst pool for cheaper throughput; autoscaler prefers reserved first. Bootstrap secret will be fetched in cloud-init via aws ssm get-parameter (SecureString) and decrypted with a KMS key — we already have a KMS key per-env.

bryan: Minor nit: the tf snippet uses aws_instance; are we doing mixed nodegroups (eks node group / managed node group) or ASGs? If EKS managed, capacity_reservation_specification might not attach the same way. For managed nodegroups we usually configure launch_template with reservation.

anya: Ah good catch — it's actually a launch_template attached to the managed node group. The snippet was simplified. Real change will be in aws_launch_template with capacity_reservation_specification block and then launch_template in aws_eks_node_group.

ops-lucy: Also make sure you taint the reserved nodes with:```yaml
node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: reserved-gpu
``` so workloads with strict latency can pin. Spot pool should be labeled like `gpu:spot` and tolerate the taint.

sre-jen: On secrets wiring, prefer SSM + KMS over storing plaintext in tfstate. Use data.aws_eks_cluster_auth? Also add IAM role for nodes to decrypt the SSM param. Example in bootstrap:```bash
aws ssm get-parameter --name /redwood/gpu/bootstrap --with-decryption --region $REGION | jq -r .Parameter.Value > /etc/kube/bootstrap.json
```

michael: For instance types: are we locking to one family (p4d) or allowing a small set for fallback? If we allow multiple, autoscaler and capacity reservations become trickier. I'd prefer primary p4d CR + fallback node group with g5.

anya: Plan: primary nodegroup = p4d w/ CR; fallback nodegroup = g5dn spot. Will add node labels and autoscaler priority. I'll update the launch_template and shared IAM module.

bryan: Remember to add `create_before_destroy = true` on the nodegroup resource so we don't evict everything during rollout.

anya: Will do. One last ask — anyone want to review the full PR? I'll push the branch in ~30m. @michael @bryan @ops-lucy

deploy-bot: CI pipeline passed for branch anya/gpu-cr-bootstrap (plan only). :white_check_mark:

michael: I'll take a look after standup. :thumbsup:

ops-lucy: Ping me if you need the taint/affinity snippets, I'll paste them into the pr.

sre-jen: Quick reminder to add audit log entry & KMS key policy update in the PR for the new key usage.

anya: Thanks all — will update the PR with launch_template, nodegroup settings, SSM wiring, and IAM roles. Back in ~45m with link.
